title: Transfer-Accept Account Ledger
prompt:
Build an in-memory `TransferLedger`. A transfer reserves money when it is requested and credits the destination only after acceptance.

- `open(account_id, initial_balance=0)` creates an account; `balance(account_id)` returns its available balance.
- `create_transfer(source, destination, amount)` reserves the amount from the source's available balance and records a pending transfer. If funds are insufficient, raise an error without changing state or consuming an ID. Successful requests return `transfer-1`, `transfer-2`, ... in creation order.
- `accept(transfer_id) -> bool` credits the reserved amount to the destination, marks the transfer `accepted`, and returns `True`. Do not debit the source a second time.
- `cancel(transfer_id)` releases the reservation back to the source and marks the transfer `cancelled`. Accepted or cancelled transfers are terminal; reject further acceptance or cancellation.
- `merge_accounts(keep, absorb)` combines available balances and removes `absorb`. Rewrite its endpoints in pending transfers to `keep`. Cancel any transfer that becomes a self-transfer and release its reserved funds into `keep`. Other reservations remain pending. Leave terminal records unchanged.
- `transfer(transfer_id)` returns a copy with `id`, `source`, `destination`, `amount`, and `status`.

Account IDs are nonempty strings, opening balances are nonnegative integers, and transfer amounts are positive integers. Transfers require distinct existing accounts. Reject malformed inputs, unknown IDs, and invalid merges. This single-threaded version uses explicit cancellation; automatic expiry and historical balance queries are follow-up discussion topics. Invalid inputs may be rejected with `assert`.

example.reasoning: Creating the transfer reserves five from ana, leaving four available. Acceptance credits bo without another debit.

references.label: Notion interview record; explicit cancellation and merge redirection are practice conventions
